findings.text: B3's witness should pin the plausible wrong validators, not only one bad value. Assert RangeError specifically for 0, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, undefined and the string '3'. A check written as `n <= 0 || n % 1 !== 0` coerces '3' and would return a page id, and it lets undefined through only by accident of NaN comparison. Also assert a boundary success at n=1. Number.isInteger plus n > 0 rejects all of these; the experiment ran a scratch model of that validator, since src/page-id.js does not exist yet.

findings.text: B1's 'imports rather than re-implements' cannot be shown by a simple-title test such as 'Hello World', because a local `toLowerCase().replace(...)` also passes it. Use titles that exercise slugify's contract: 'Café' gives 'caf-1' and 'a_b' gives 'a-b-1', with edge-hyphen and separator-run inputs as well. The import itself remains a read-at-gate check on src/page-id.js. B2 should also cover '' as well as '!!!', since both slugify to empty and fall back to 'page'.

Spec gap, not a build blocker: for very large integers, string concatenation gives exponent notation. pageId('a', 1e21) would return 'a-1e+21', and Number.isInteger(1e21) is true, so B3 does not reject it. Values above 2^53 also pass with imprecise digits. The contract only says 'positive integer', so Number.isInteger is a conforming reading, and Number.isSafeInteger would be a stricter choice that the contract does not state. The builder should not widen behaviour on its own. If the root wants ids to stay decimal-only, that takes a contract amendment.

reasons: The spec's premises hold at this tip: slugify exists and returns '' for empty slugs, so B2's fallback belongs in pageId. Acceptance B1-B4 matches contract one with no drift, and the page-id lane argv fits C-2's one-test-file-per-module rule. The existing suite passes (6 tests). Findings are notes on witness strength and one unstated large-integer edge.

premises.claim: F1 holds at this checkout: src/slug.js exports slugify. The commit is on integration, not yet on main, which is still at b819cd9, so the unit must build on the integration line.
slugify has no empty-result fallback, so the 'page' fallback is pageId's responsibility and no slug change is needed.
C-1 and C-2 require a pure module with no dependencies and one test file per module, which src/page-id.js and test/page-id.test.js satisfy as scoped.
